# IPTV EPG Search

A client-side web app for searching IPTV Electronic Program Guide (EPG) data (XMLTV) and for browsing an
online cinema catalogue (M3U playlists). The TV Guide tab does fuzzy search with Russian/English stemming and
can open a channel's live or catch-up stream in a new tab; the Cinema tab groups episodes into series.
Everything runs in the browser as plain JavaScript with no build step; one Vercel serverless function proxies
provider requests to get around CORS.

> Status: **implemented and in use.** TV Guide search (fuzzy search, channel filter, ratings), the Cinema tab,
> and the Watch Live and Catch-up buttons (Phases 1–2 of the Live TV plan) are built. Only the rating and
> fuzzy-search logic have tests, and those run in the browser.
> [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) is the authoritative design source;
> [docs/design/live-tv-playback-plan.md](docs/design/live-tv-playback-plan.md) records the Live TV and
> catch-up design.
>
> Build & test: `npm run dev` (local server), `node --check <file>` (syntax check; no linter or typecheck is
> configured), the browser test page `tests/test-runner.html` (serve the repo root, see Tooling),
> `npm run deploy` (production; only when asked).

## Read before making changes

1. [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) — system structure, components, stability zones.
2. The relevant `AI_*.md` file(s) for the code you are touching — always use `AI*.md` for coding rules (see below).
3. `docs/chats/` — previous talks and implementations.
4. The documentation in the root and in `docs/` (`README.md`, `docs/design/`, the guides).

## Working agreement

- **Never start code right after USER question/message. Propose solution and ask for explicit request for implementation.**
  The same goes for any other change to files and for any state-changing command; reading, searching,
  analyzing and answering need no confirmation. If the user says "just do it" / "go ahead", proceed directly.
- **Never stage and commit. Only User can do this.**
- Follow all applicable `AI*.md` files strictly, and document architecture as-is, not as imagined.
- **Never weaken URL and HTML sanitization (`utils/sanitize.js`), the proxy's protocol and content-type
  checks, or the timezone-correct time handling just to make a feature or a check pass; surface the honest
  failure instead.**
- **Verify against the provider's real data, don't assume.** Before changing how EPG (XMLTV) or playlist (M3U)
  data is parsed, or how Live and Catch-up URLs are built (`?utc=…&lutc=…`), check it against
  [docs/design/live-tv-playback-plan.md](docs/design/live-tv-playback-plan.md) §5 (the probed server
  behaviour) and the sample files in `tmp/` (`playlist.m3u`, `channels-iptv.xml`; git-ignored, local only) —
  not memory or inference. Cite the file you checked so the claim is checkable.
- **Verify against this codebase — don't describe it from memory.** Every factual claim about how
  _this project_ behaves — a file path, which fields a component renders, when a code path actually
  runs, a payload or API shape, a config key — must be read out of the source before it is stated.
  This applies to **prose as much as to code**: answers, design docs, test plans, and manual steps
  handed to the user. Prose is where the errors concentrate, because `node --check` and the browser test page
  (`tests/test-runner.html`) catch a wrong edit but never catch a wrong sentence. Recurring traps:
  `program.start` / `program.stop` ignore the timezone offset (use `startRaw` and `epgRawToEpochSeconds` for
  anything absolute); `npm run dev` serves only `public/`, so `api/proxy.js` and `tests/` are not reachable
  through it; `escapeHtml` / `escapeAttr` / `sanitizeUrl` exist as local copies in `cinemaTab.js` (and
  `escapeHtml` in `results.js` and `channelFilter.js`) next to the shared `utils/sanitize.js`. Start from
  `public/scripts/main.js` (it wires every module) and grep `public/scripts/` for the symbol before
  describing it. Cite `file:line` so the claim is checkable. Having built the thing in this same session is
  **not** verification — that memory is exactly what drifts.
- **Stop and ask** if anything is unclear or contradictory.

## Tooling

- **Client** — plain JavaScript (ES modules) in the browser; no build step, bundler, TypeScript or CommonJS.
  Third-party libraries are local files in `public/vendor/`. Check each touched file with
  `node --check <file>` (Node is installed locally; no linter, formatter or typecheck is configured).
- **Proxy** — `api/proxy.js`, a Vercel Serverless Function written as an ES module (`"type": "module"`).
- **Local server** — `npm run dev` runs `python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory public`. It serves only
  `public/`: `api/` does not run, so on `localhost` the app fetches provider URLs directly.
- **Tests** — browser-based, no command-line runner. Serve the repo root (`python3 -m http.server 8000`) and
  open `/tests/test-runner.html`.
- **Deploy** — `npm run deploy` (`vercel --prod`) publishes to production; run it only when the user asks.
- **Secrets** — none; the app needs no environment variables, and `.env*` files are git-ignored. No database,
  backend framework, React, TypeScript or Docker is part of this project.
